top_signals.title: Patterson: For now, Iran has won the war
top_signals.summary: With the Iran war appearing to de-escalate, energy-market pressure may linger. Iran could retain greater influence over the Strait of Hormuz, keeping shipping and insurance costs elevated even as oil flows resume. Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders and Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson join Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about their new book “Investment Wisdom,” how higher fuel and refined-product costs may feed inflation, complicate the Fed’s path and weigh on the economy. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Fed's Collins Says Additional Policy Tightening Is Appropriate
top_signals.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins says recent data show inflation is too high and broadening. Speaking with Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Collins adds that because of the increasing inflation risks, more rate tightening is needed. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: The Record Budgets and Missing Suppliers Shaping America’s Munitions Ramp
top_signals.summary:
The Pentagon is sending a record demand signal for munitions, but turning it into deliveries depends on suppliers several tiers below the primes, many of which disappeared over the last two decades. Marc Andersen (Army assistant secretary and chief investment officer of the Strategic Capital Initiative), Brandon Daniels (Exiger), and Joseph “Gus” Guastella (Voyager Technologies) join Jonathan in the studio. They debate whether China’s control of critical minerals could halt U.S. munitions production and discuss the Army’s strategic capital initiative, the Patriot production ramp, and the push for cheaper munitions.Image: Christine Mitchell via DVIDS.

top_signals.title: Finance Experts Reveal Lessons for Investors
top_signals.summary: In a world of 24/7 trading, options and investing apps, Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders and Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson join Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about their new book, “Investment Wisdom for Our Friends and Loved Ones: Timeless Lessons from Today’s Top Finance Experts.” They share timeless advice: start early, harness the power of compounding, and know the difference between investing and gambling. alerts.title: Trump Is Facing a Very Different North Korea
alerts.summary: Donald Trump has Pyongyang on his mind. In recent months, the U.S. president has made comments to the media suggesting he is in communication with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. In an August 17 Truth Social post, for instance, Trump announced that the United States would scale back joint military drills with South Korea. The decision, he wrote, was “based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong Un,” describing the dictator as “unthreatening and respectful.”
